questions.question: If a trailer starts to skid, what should the driver do?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel quickly left, then right.

questions.explanation: If your trailer starts to skid, release the brakes. The trailer will straighten out when the wheels grip the road again.

questions.question: What is the best way to check your lights during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Park near a mirror and look for a reflection.
Turn on the lights, then get out and look at them.
Check the instrument panel for warning lights.
Drive in traffic and wait for other drivers to signal if your lights are out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on the lights, then get out and look at them.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, turn on your lights and exit the vehicle to look at them.

questions.question: When entering traffic with a double or triple, drivers should know that these vehicles:

options.text: Need more space to merge than smaller vehicles.
Are not subject to most speed limits.
Are hard for other drivers to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need more space to merge than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Doubles and triples are longer and heavier than other vehicles. They cannot turn or stop quickly. Always make sure you have enough space before entering traffic, crossing traffic, or changing lanes.

questions.question: Alcohol leaves your body:
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a steady rate. Coffee, cold showers, and other tricks do not speed this up. The only way to become sober is to give your body time to remove the alcohol.

questions.question: When changing lanes, should you use your turn signal?

options.text: Only use it if there is traffic.
Only use it between dusk and dawn.

questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes.

questions.question: Do not decide when to shift gears based on:

options.text: The speed shown on your speedometer (mph).
What the vehicle next to you is doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: What the vehicle next to you is doing.
questions.explanation: Shift up when your engine reaches the top of its operating range. You can also shift based on your speedometer reading. Learn which speeds work best for each gear.

questions.question: When starting from a stop, a vehicle should:
questions.explanation: Make sure your vehicle does not roll backward when starting from a complete stop. This helps prevent hitting vehicles or objects behind you.

questions.question: A distracted driver may be:

options.text: Not talking to anyone in the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Signs of a distracted driver include drifting within a lane, changing speeds, using a cell phone, reading a map, eating, or talking to passengers.

questions.question: A driver who stops at a green light could be:
questions.explanation: Watch for signs that another driver may be impaired. Drivers who have drunk alcohol, are tired, are using drugs, or are sick can be dangerous. Stopping at green lights is one sign a driver may be impaired.

questions.question: Federal and state laws require drivers to:

options.text: Inspect their vehicles only if they think something is wrong.
Inspect their vehicles only when traveling out-of-state.
Inspect their vehicles only when carrying hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: Commercial drivers must inspect their vehicles before every trip. Regular inspections help drivers find problems before they become dangerous or expensive.

questions.question: If you turn to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do not brake. Braking can lock the wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not brake. Braking can lock the wheels.
questions.explanation: Do not brake while turning quickly to avoid a hazard. Braking can lock your wheels and cause your vehicle to skid out of control.

questions.question: Air brakes use ____ to work.
questions.explanation: Air brake systems use compressed air to function.

questions.question: Why should you do routine vehicle inspections?
questions.explanation: The main reason to inspect your vehicle is safety. Regular inspections protect you and other road users.

questions.question: What should you check about leaf springs?
questions.explanation: Check that leaf springs have no missing or broken leaves. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing, the vehicle cannot be driven until it is fixed.

questions.question: What does ABS on only one axle do?

options.text: Gives you better control when braking.
Slows the vehicle, but cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you better control when braking.
questions.explanation: Even if your Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is on only one axle, it still gives you more control when braking than you would have without it. Brake normally.

questions.question: If you double your speed from 20 to 40 mph, your braking distance will become ____ times longer.
questions.explanation: When you double your speed, your braking distance becomes four times longer. The force of a collision also multiplies by four.

questions.question: When brakes create too much heat, what can happen?
questions.explanation: If brakes get too hot, they may fade and lose their stopping power. Do not rely only on brakes. Also use engine braking to slow your vehicle.

questions.question: What causes brake fade?
questions.explanation: Overusing brakes causes them to overheat and lose effectiveness. This is called brake fade.

questions.question: What does rust around wheel nuts mean?
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts can mean they are loose. Check that the nuts are tight if you see rust.

questions.question: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under a bridge or sign, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit, slow down. Take a different route if possible.
